PullRequest.Title: sessions: use filled circles for PR artifact progress
PullRequest.Body:

Replaces sync codicons with filled circles for pending/in-progress PR artifact check summaries and individual checks, preserving existing colors. Updates the PR loading-state fixture and test expectations consistently.

## Validation

- `fnm exec --using 24.22.1 pnpm run build-fast --client-only` — passed.
- `fnm exec --using 24.22.1 ./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/githubPullRequestArtifactIntegration.test.ts --reporter dot` — passed, 102 tests.
- `fnm exec --using 24.22.1 pnpm run oxlint src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/artifactIntegrations/githubPullRequestArtifactIntegration.ts src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/githubPullRequestArtifactIntegration.test.ts src/vs/sessions/contrib/chat/test/browser/artifactIntegrationPresentation.fixture.ts` — passed.
- Visual fixture validation was not run because the Component Explorer daemon was unavailable.

Scenarios.Scenario: A session artifact pill updates its pull-request checks summary while one or more checks are pending.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The existing GitHub pull-request subscription refresh must produce a snapshot, the artifact model must publish it to the client, and the pill autorun synchronously rebuilds the status-button content. The changed line only selects a different registered glyph ID inside the already-required snapshot derivation; it adds no blocking step.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Refresh the existing pull-request subscription with core, conversation, checks, and mergeability interests.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One logical subscription refresh for this pull request per existing refresh trigger; repository-client caching/coalescing remains unchanged.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same refresh occurred before the diff and produced the same check collection and presentation update.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: On a cold or explicitly authoritative refresh, this existing operation gates the new check state; warm observable reads reuse the current snapshot.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Publish the artifact contribution snapshot from the agent host to the client.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: The existing update count is unchanged; the pending summary contains one icon ID, now `circle-filled-compact` rather than `sync-compact`.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same snapshot update was sent with an identically shaped icon object and the shorter prior glyph ID.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The existing snapshot delivery gates client rendering, but the diff introduces no additional message or round trip.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One checks-summary button per pull request artifact, independent of check count; computing existing check states remains O(number of checks), and the glyph substitution does not change that work.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Artifact model refreshes are already serialized by the existing sequencer, while UI presentation runs once per observable snapshot update; the diff changes neither concurrency nor backpressure.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The pull-request subscription and current observable snapshot retain their existing warm-cache behavior, cache keys, invalidation, and coalescing. The icon ID does not participate in any cache key.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence: both IDs are registered codicons, pass through the same icon-registry lookup, and render as one DOM glyph; no spin modifier is attached.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The exact GitHub refresh latency and number of simultaneously visible artifacts vary, but neither is affected by the diff. The new ID is nine ASCII characters longer in one summary object, which is not a realistic user-visible serialization regression.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. CPU, DOM node count, layout behavior, network cardinality, IPC cardinality, and retained state are unchanged.

Scenarios.Scenario: A user opens pull-request artifact details containing pending individual checks.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The existing details request builds a page of at most 200 check items, transports it to the client, and the virtualized details list renders visible rows. Each pending item invokes the same `checkIcon` helper, but the replacement remains one registry lookup and one glyph element per rendered row.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Return a paged artifact-details payload containing check items and their icon descriptors.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most 200 items per existing details page; one icon descriptor per item. A fully pending page carries up to about 1.8 KB of additional uncompressed identifier text, with no extra request or item.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same number of items and icon descriptors crossed the boundary using `sync-compact`; paging was already capped at 200.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The existing details response gates first-page display. The glyph substitution does not alter paging, request count, or renderer work.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Use the existing pull-request subscription, promoted to interactive priority while details are leased, to supply check data.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One existing subscription for the pull request; opening details changes its pre-existing priority rather than issuing per-check network calls.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical subscription interests, priority, and refresh behavior.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Cold check data can gate details, while warm snapshots render without a new fetch. The diff does not move or add this boundary.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Pending checks in the requested page, capped at 200 after paging; actual DOM work scales with virtualized visible rows. The diff changes only the icon ID string, not effective item cardinality.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One paged details request is handled through the existing model/transport path; checks are mapped synchronously and no per-check asynchronous work or concurrency burst is introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The existing pull-request snapshot is reused while warm, detail leases retain the same subscription, and page boundaries remain unchanged. No positive, negative, or icon cache behavior changes.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence: the page cap and per-row rendering path are explicit, and both old and new values create the same ArtifactIcon shape and DOM structure.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Transport encoding and compression can reduce or alter the exact byte delta, but the strict upper-bound string increase is tiny and does not establish measurable latency, CPU, or GC impact.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The only scaling delta is a bounded, negligible identifier-length increase; boundary count, CPU shape, and rendering cardinality are unchanged.

Scenarios.Scenario: The Component Explorer/test fixture renders a pull-request artifact in its loading state.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: An in-memory fixture creates one availability section and the existing artifact presentation renders one glyph. No product startup, remote refresh, or asynchronous data dependency is added.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: One local fixture section per preview instance.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous local fixture construction and rendering only; no queue, limiter, IPC, filesystem, subprocess, database, or network activity.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache is involved; both glyphs are already statically registered codicons.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from the fixture implementation and shared renderer path.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: None material: this changed file is test/preview data rather than production data acquisition.
Scenarios.Verdict: No performance regression; the preview substitutes one glyph for another with identical element cardinality.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all three changed files and all diff pages. The production change replaces one registered codicon ID in existing summary and paged-item presentation paths; tests and fixture expectations follow it. Rendering, refresh scheduling, network/IPC call counts, paging, cache lifecycle, concurrency, DOM cardinality, and animation behavior remain unchanged, so there are no actionable performance findings and no evidenced shipped-regression fix to record.
